driver_help: Build the Rust implementation of the null block driver.
This target is currently used as a calibration-only Rust block-driver benchmark.

null_blk.h.reason: The calibration workflow targets the Rust block/configfs abstractions rather than porting the private `null_blk.h` helper surface into bindgen or translated Rust.
null_blk.h.rust_strategy: Model the required behavior through the block-mq/configfs abstraction plan and the official `rnull` surface instead of landing this private header.

translation.goal: Calibrate the toolchain around `drivers/block/null_blk/main.c -> drivers/block/rnull/rnull.rs` by describing the official Rust `rnull` module through strict block/configfs artifacts before any blind-first migration attempt.
translation.abstraction_goal: Constrain the current `rnull` phase to the official block-mq plus configfs subset so the tool can validate blk-mq request flow, configfs-powered device lifecycle, and Kbuild/runtime contracts without overstating blind migration support.

mvp_scope.note: This profile is calibration-only: it should validate the official Rust driver shape and the tool contracts for create/destroy plus minimal I/O smoke before any blind-first `null_blk` experiment.

body_plan: Map the queue callback to `block::mq::Operations::queue_rq` using `QueueData` as the only per-queue state.
Preserve the calibrated split between synchronous completion (`Request::end_ok`) and softirq completion (`Request::complete`) without exposing raw request ownership to driver code.
Finish asynchronously completed requests through the typed `Request` API only.
Keep the expectation that the final request reference is unique at completion inside the abstraction-owned request type.
Create the per-device configfs group through `configfs::Group::new` and owned Rust state.
Seed the calibration subset fields (`power`, `block_size`, `rotational`, `capacity_mib`, `irq_mode`, `disk`) inside an owned mutex-backed Rust struct.
Report the supported configfs calibration attributes as a static text list through a typed page writer.
Render the current powered state from owned Rust state without exposing raw configfs data pointers.
Translate power-on into `NullBlkDevice::new(...)` and store the resulting `GenDisk` inside owned Rust state.
Translate power-off into `guard.disk.take()` plus state update, keeping teardown best-effort and owned.
Expose the configured block size through a typed formatter.
Reject writes while powered, validate block size through `GenDiskBuilder::validate_block_size`, and then update owned Rust state.
Expose the current rotational flag through a typed formatter.
Reject writes while powered and update the typed boolean configuration through `kstrtobool_bytes`.
Expose the configured capacity in MiB through a typed formatter.
Reject writes while powered and parse the configured capacity into owned Rust state.
Expose the current IRQ mode through the typed Rust enum formatter.
Reject writes while powered, parse the mode as an integer, and convert it through `IRQMode::try_from`.

private_state.layout: Configfs-owned device state guarded by a Rust mutex, with the created disk owned as `Option<GenDisk<NullBlkDevice>>`.

fields.name: powered
fields.role: Track whether the configfs device is currently powered on.

fields.name: name
fields.role: Persist the configfs device name for disk creation.

fields.name: block_size
fields.role: Own the configured logical/physical block size.

fields.name: irq_mode
fields.role: Own the calibrated IRQ completion mode.

fields.name: disk
fields.role: Own the live disk while powered on and drop it during power-off or group teardown.

private_state.note: The calibration subset keeps per-device state entirely on the configfs side; advanced null_blk runtime state remains outside this phase.

runtime_expectation.scope: create/destroy plus minimal I/O smoke only
